newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Buenos Aires prov. may call new tender for utility.
newsitem.headline: Buenos Aires prov. may call new tender for utility.

text.p: Buenos Aires province utility ESEBA may call a new tender, probably in December, to sell its electricity generation area after receiving Monday an unacceptable bid, ESEBA's President Jose Romero said Tuesday.
"We are considering calling a new tender in December," Romero told Reuters.
A consortium headed by Italy's Camuzzi and also formed by local CEI Citicorp Holdings SA was the only bidder for ESEBA's generation units with an offer of $19.7 million.

After selling earlier this month the distribution business of ESEBA for $1.1 billion, more than what they had expected, Buenos Aires officials said they saw the generation area going for more than the $100 million technicians had estimated.
"The price offered was too low," Romero said. "The group tried to get a bargain instead of paying a real price."

The other firm that qualified for ESEBA's generation units was Argentine thermoelectric generator Central Costanera, but it did not show up at Monday's tender. Central Costanera is 51 percent owned by Chile's ENDESA, controlled in turn by Chile's ENERSIS SA.
Romero said ESEBA "will launch a drive to clinch long-term contracts at reasonable prices with major industrial consumers to make it more attractive for the private sector.
"We will try to take advantage of ESEBA's strategic situation," he said.
One of the two generation units of ESEBA is located in the southern Buenos Aires port of Bahia Blanca where a huge petrochemical complex is also located.
